spec.description: ktranslate collector health (--metrics=jchf): SNMP, flow, sFlow, traps, syslog. OTLP labels (service_name). Aligned with NR container health guide.

spec.title: Total Upload Errors
spec.description: All failed metric upload attempts in the selected time range.

spec.title: Device Polling Health (Prometheus)
spec.description: PollingHealth value per device. Non-1 or missing values indicate the device is not being polled successfully.

spec.title: Device Uptime and Status (Prometheus)
spec.description: Device uptime and polling status from Prometheus. Devices missing here are not sending any metrics.

options.content:
## KTranslate Health Dashboard

Monitors **ktranslate** collector containers polling SNMP devices in this lab. Use the **Container** dropdown to filter panels to a specific container.

**Reading the stats above:** all four error counters should be zero. Work top-to-bottom — upload failures drop entire batches before they reach Prometheus; 0-interface counts mean individual devices are reachable but returning nothing useful.

> Container IDs change on every recycle. The **Container** variable auto-discovers active containers from Loki logs.

### ResourceExhausted — batch too large
ktranslate packed too many metrics into one gRPC call and the Alloy receiver rejected it (default 4 MB limit). Devices with hundreds of interfaces blow up batch sizes fast.

**Fix — choose one:**
1. **Increase Alloy limit** → set `max_recv_msg_size_mib = 16` in the `otelcol.receiver.otlp` block.
2. **Reduce ktranslate batch size** → lower `--max_flows_per_message` in the container command.
3. **Split large devices** → move high-interface-count devices into a dedicated low-device-count container.

---
### Invalid UTF-8 — bad encoding in a device field
A device OID (often `sysDescr`, `ifAlias`, or `sysContact`) returned a non-UTF-8 byte sequence. ktranslate cannot JSON-marshal it and drops the metric.

**Fix:**
1. Find the device → search Loki: `{service_name=~"ktranslate.*|integrations/ktranslate-netflow"} |= "invalid UTF-8"` — the device name usually appears in the same log line.
2. Identify the field → look for the OID or field name preceding the error.
3. Exclude that OID in the ktranslate SNMP profile for that device type, or sanitise it with a `string_strip` transform in the profile.

### 🔴 Devices returning 0 interfaces
ktranslate reached the device via SNMP (it didn't time out) but `IF-MIB::ifTable` came back empty. The device is up; the problem is access control or profile selection.

**Common causes and fixes:**

| Cause | Fix |
|---|---|
| Wrong SNMP community or v3 credentials | Re-check `snmp-devices.yaml` for the device entry; test with `snmpget -v2c -c <community> <ip> sysDescr.0` |
| Device ACL blocks `ifTable` OID range | Add `1.3.6.1.2.1.2` to the device's SNMP allowed-OID list |
| Wrong ktranslate profile for device type | Check container logs for `"matched profile"` lines; compare against [kentik/snmp-profiles](https://github.com/kentik/snmp-profiles/tree/main/profiles/kentik_snmp) |
| Interface table lives under a vendor MIB, not IF-MIB | Add a `table` override in the device's ktranslate profile pointing to the vendor OID |

**Quick manual test:** `snmpwalk -v2c -c <community> <device_ip> IF-MIB::ifTable` — if this returns nothing, the problem is on the device side.

### Reading the Prometheus tables

**Device Polling Health** — lists every device with `kentik_snmp_PollingHealth = 1` currently reaching Prometheus. A device absent from this table has a complete pipeline break somewhere upstream.

**Device Uptime & Status** — SNMP uptime confirms the device is reachable. Cross-reference with Polling Health:
- **High uptime + in Polling Health** → healthy ✅
- **High uptime + missing from Polling Health** → device is up but ktranslate is not delivering its metrics (check Upload Failures panels for the container that polls this device)
- **Missing from both tables** → ktranslate may not be polling it at all, or polls are failing silently

### Tracing a missing device end-to-end
1. Find the container → search Loki for the device name to see which `host_name` emits logs for it.
2. Check that container's upload failure rate in the **Upload Failures by Container** panel.
3. If ResourceExhausted errors are spiking on that container, the entire batch (including this device) is being dropped before Alloy.
4. Fix the batch size issue first — once uploads succeed, the device should appear in the Polling Health table within one poll interval.

spec.title: Input Queue Depth by Container
spec.description: Messages waiting in the input queue. Non-zero and rising means ktranslate cannot process data fast enough.

spec.title: Output Queue Depth by Container
spec.description: Messages waiting to be sent to the output sink. Rising values here indicate the upstream pipeline is outpacing delivery.

spec.title: JCHF Buffer Depth
spec.description: Compact flow header queue capacity. Value of 8000 means the buffer is saturated — flow data may be dropped. Lower values indicate data flowing freely.

spec.title: Syslog Queue Depth
spec.description: Current depth of the syslog processing queue. Should be near 0; sustained values indicate the syslog pipeline is backing up.

spec.title: ResourceExhausted Errors
spec.description: Batch too large — gRPC message exceeds 4 MB receiver limit.

options.content:
### Processing Queues — OTLP label: `service_name`

Maps [New Relic ktranslate health metrics](https://docs.newrelic.com/docs/network-performance-monitoring/advanced/ktranslate-container-health/) to **OTLP/Prometheus** (`kentik_ktranslate_chf_kkc_*`) with `--metrics=jchf --sinks=otel`:

| NR / ktranslate CHF | Grafana (OTLP) | What to watch |
|---|---|---|
| `baseserver_healthcheck_execution_total` | `..._baseserver_healthcheck_execution_total` | Must be > 0 |
| `inputq` / `inputq_len` | `..._inputq` / `..._inputq_len` | Arrival rate; backlog ≈ 0 |
| `jchfq` | `..._jchfq` | Buffer headroom (~8000 max) |
| `device_metrics` | `..._device_metrics` | SNMP pollers only |
| `netflow.flows` | `..._netflow_flows` | Flow/sFlow containers |
| `syslog_*` | `..._syslog_queue/messages/errors` | Syslog container |
| `delivery_logs_otel` | `..._delivery_logs_otel` | Logs/sec to Alloy |

**Facet by `service_name`:** `ktranslate-snmp-*`, `ktranslate-syslog-*`, `ktranslate-flow-*`, `ktranslate-sflow-*`. Flow rollups use datapoint label `integration=ktranslate-netflow` (not `service_name`).

**Logs:** `--tee_logs=true` → Loki with the same `service_name` labels.

spec.title: Healthcheck Execution Time (mean / p99 / max)
spec.description: Healthcheck loop execution time per container, summarized to worst-observed mean / p99 / max (ms) over the selected window. Raw metric exposes mean/p99/min/max as labels on every sample (not separate series), so this aggregates them into one row per container instead of ~100 noisy near-duplicate lines.

spec.expression: SELECT service_name AS container_service, MAX(CAST(mean AS DOUBLE))/100 AS mean_ms, MAX(CAST(key_99_percentile AS DOUBLE))/100 AS p99_ms, MAX(CAST(max AS DOUBLE))/100 AS max_ms FROM A GROUP BY service_name

spec.title: Healthcheck Rate by Container
spec.description: Rate of healthcheck executions per second per container. A flat or dropping line means the container's health loop has stalled.

options.content:
### Healthcheck Performance — reading the signals

The **baseserver healthcheck** is ktranslate's internal liveness loop — a recurring self-test that confirms the core goroutines are alive and the pipeline is moving data.

| Signal | Healthy | Investigate |
|---|---|---|
| **execution_time (mean)** | Stable, low ms | Sustained upward drift → CPU/IO bottleneck |
| **execution_time (p99 / max)** | Close to mean | Spiky excursions → GC pauses or lock contention |
| **execution_rate** | Flat, consistent | Falling or zero → container loop has stalled or crashed |

The time series uses the labels exposed directly by ktranslate: `min`, `mean`, `max`, `five_minute`, `fifteen_minute`, `key_99_percentile`. If mean climbs while p99 stays flat, the load is uniformly high; if p99 spikes while mean stays low, you have bursty delays.

spec.title: Device Polling Status
spec.description: PollingStatus per device — complements PollingHealth. Non-1 values indicate the device is not being polled successfully.

spec.title: SNMP Errors by Device
spec.description: SNMP request errors per device (transport/protocol-level failures). Non-zero and rising indicates the container can't reliably reach these devices.

spec.title: SNMP Poll Health by Device (snmp_fail)
spec.description: SNMP poll health gauge per device (kentik_ktranslate_chf_kkc_snmp_fail). **1 = healthy**; values > 1 indicate failure modes. Requires --metrics=jchf.

spec.title: SNMP Missing Responses by Device
spec.description: SNMP requests sent with no corresponding response per device. Distinct from fail/error — indicates dropped requests or unreachable OIDs.

spec.title: Device Metrics Collected by Device
spec.description: Volume of device-level metrics collected per poll cycle, by device. A drop toward zero means that device stopped contributing data.

spec.title: Interface Metrics Collected by Device
spec.description: Volume of interface-level metrics collected per poll cycle, by device. A drop toward zero means that device's interfaces stopped reporting.

spec.title: SNMP Traps Received by Device
spec.description: SNMP traps received per device. Confirms the trap listener is alive and devices are sending unsolicited events.

spec.title: Syslog Messages Received by Device
spec.description: Syslog messages received per device. Confirms the syslog listener is alive and devices are actively sending logs.

spec.title: Syslog Errors by Device
spec.description: Syslog processing errors per device — parsing/ingest failures on the syslog pipeline, separate from metric upload failures.

spec.title: Container Startup Args (KTranslate CLI)
spec.description: Startup CLI invocation per container, showing every flag ktranslate launched with. Useful for confirming config/version drift between containers.

spec.title: Input Message Rate by Container
spec.description: Top-level input throughput per container — messages/sec received from all SNMP, flow, and syslog inputs combined. Distinct from Input Queue Depth (backlog); this is the arrival rate.

spec.title: Log Delivery Rate by Container
spec.description: Logs/sec successfully delivered to the OTel collector per container. A flat-zero line while syslog_messages is non-zero indicates delivery is failing downstream.

spec.title: Devices Returning 0 Interfaces
spec.description: Devices that polled successfully but returned no interface metrics — likely an SNMP auth or profile mismatch.

spec.title: KTranslate Containers (CHF heartbeat)
spec.description: Per-container build version and last CHF heartbeat via baseserver_healthcheck_execution_total (OTLP service_name label).

spec.expression: SELECT A.service_name AS container_service, A.ver AS ver, B.__value__*1000 AS last_seen FROM A JOIN B ON A.service_name=B.service_name LIMIT 100

spec.title: KTranslate Health Summary (per container)
spec.description: Equivalent to: FROM Metric SELECT latest(healthcheck_total), latest(input_per_second), latest(buffer) FACET host, svc WHERE provider='kentik-agent' AND instrumentation.name='heartbeat'. One row per container process, latest reported values.

spec.expression: SELECT A.service_name AS container_service, A.__value__ AS healthcheck_total, B.__value__ AS input_per_second, C.__value__ AS buffer FROM A JOIN B ON A.service_name = B.service_name JOIN C ON A.service_name = C.service_name LIMIT 100

spec.title: SNMP Polling Health (per container)
spec.description: Equivalent to: FROM Metric SELECT latest(device_metrics), latest(interface_metrics) FACET host, svc WHERE provider='kentik-agent' AND instrumentation.name='heartbeat'. SNMP polling throughput per container — zero or dropping values mean that container has stopped polling devices.

spec.expression: SELECT A.service_name AS container_service, A.__value__ AS device_polls_per_second, B.__value__ AS interface_polls_per_second FROM A JOIN B ON A.service_name = B.service_name LIMIT 100

spec.title: Devices Failing SNMP Polling
spec.description: Devices with snmp_fail > 1 (failure codes 3–9) in the last 6h. Value 1 means healthy; see ktranslate SNMP_GOOD/SNMP_BAD_* constants.

spec.expression: SELECT service_name AS container_service, device_name AS snmp_device, __value__ AS snmp_fail FROM A WHERE __value__ > 1 LIMIT 100

spec.title: Syslog Health (per container)
spec.description: Syslog queue depth, error rate, and message rate per container (last heartbeat, 6h window)

spec.expression: SELECT A.service_name AS container_service, A.__value__ AS syslog_queue_total, B.__value__ AS syslog_errors_per_second, C.__value__ AS syslog_messages_per_second FROM A JOIN B ON A.service_name=B.service_name JOIN C ON A.service_name=C.service_name LIMIT 100

options.content:
## KTranslate Health Dashboard

Monitors **ktranslate** collector containers (SNMP, flow, sFlow, syslog) via CHF metrics (`kentik_ktranslate_chf_kkc_*`). Use the **Collector (service_name)** dropdown to filter panels.

**Reading the stats above:** upload error counters should be zero. Role stat row confirms flow/syslog CHF is live after the OTLP jchf fix.

## Device Polling — are containers actively polling devices via SNMP?

Covers per-device and per-container SNMP poll activity: poll rate, errors, timeouts, missing responses, and devices returning zero interfaces. Use this tab to diagnose devices that are unreachable or misconfigured — wrong community string/credentials, an ACL blocking the poller, or the wrong device profile.

## Metrics Pipeline — what data is landing in Prometheus?

SNMP (`device_metrics`), syslog (`syslog_messages`), and flow (`netflow_flows` CHF + `network_io_by_flow_bytes{integration="ktranslate-netflow"}` rollup). Use the **role stat row** on Overview and the flow/syslog panels below. Empty CHF with healthy SNMP usually means `--metrics=jchf` missing on that container or OTLP delivery gap — check **Queues & Delivery**.

## Queues & Delivery — is ktranslate keeping up, and are batches reaching the backend?

Tracks internal backpressure (input/output/JCHF/syslog queue depths, message and delivery rates) and upload/delivery failures (gRPC ResourceExhausted, per-container and per-error-type breakdowns). Rising queue depth or non-zero upload errors mean ktranslate is falling behind or being rejected downstream — even if polling and collection upstream look fine.

spec.title: Flow Health (CHF netflow_flows + Mimir rollup)
spec.description: CHF **netflow_flows** ingest per flow/sFlow container (`--metrics=jchf`). Compared with rolled-up `network_io_by_flow_bytes{integration="ktranslate-netflow"}` (Alloy tags rollups only; CHF keeps `ktranslate-flow-*` / `ktranslate-sflow-*`).

spec.title: Devices Reporting Metrics to Prometheus
spec.description: Unique device_names actively reporting kentik_snmp_PollingHealth to Prometheus. Devices absent here have no metrics landing.

spec.title: SNMP Missing Metadata by Device
spec.description: Devices where SNMP metadata collection failed (profile/OID gaps). Distinct from snmp_missing (no response) and snmp_fail (poll state).

spec.title: Active ktranslate Containers (CHF heartbeat)
spec.description: One series per container role (SNMP, flow, sFlow, syslog). Expect one line per running ktranslate process.

spec.title: Flow CHF (flows/s)
spec.description: Sum of kentik_ktranslate_chf_kkc_netflow_flows across flow/sFlow containers.

spec.title: Syslog CHF (msgs/s)
spec.description: Syslog messages/sec on ktranslate_syslog containers.

spec.title: SNMP poll throughput
spec.description: SNMP device_metrics poll rate on ktranslate-snmp containers.

spec.title: CHF containers up
spec.description: Containers reporting baseserver healthcheck CHF.

spec.title: Syslog Pipeline (CHF ingest vs OTLP delivery)
spec.description: syslog_messages = listener ingest; delivery_logs_otel = logs/sec handed to Alloy. Flat delivery with rising messages ⇒ downstream OTLP/Loki issue.

spec.title: Flow/sFlow Queue Pressure (CHF)
spec.description: inputq_len backlog and jchfq buffer headroom for flow containers only (~8000 = saturated).

spec.title: Upload Failures by Error Type
spec.description: Rate of upload failures by error type. ResourceExhausted = batch too large. UTF-8 = bad encoding in a device field.

spec.title: Upload Failures by Container
spec.description: Upload failures broken down by container. A container with consistent errors is the one not delivering data to Prometheus.

spec.expr: sum by(deployment_host) (count_over_time({service_name=~"ktranslate.*|integrations/ktranslate-netflow"} | service_name=~"$service_name" |= "failed to upload metrics" [$__auto]))

spec.title: Poll Activity by Container
spec.description: SNMP poll executions per container. A flat or missing line means that container has stopped polling.

spec.expr: sum by(deployment_host) (count_over_time({service_name=~"ktranslate.*|integrations/ktranslate-netflow"} | service_name=~"$service_name" |= "SNMP interface metric poll" [$__auto]))

spec.title: Devices with 0 Interfaces (Polling Failures)
spec.description: Devices repeatedly returning 0 interfaces. Investigate SNMP community strings, ACLs, or missing MIB profiles for these.

spec.expr: sum by(device, deployment_host) (count_over_time({service_name=~"ktranslate.*|integrations/ktranslate-netflow"} |= "found metrics for 0 interfaces" | regexp "KTranslate>(?P<device>[^ ]+) SNMP" [$__range]))

spec.title: Healthcheck Performance — is the core loop healthy?
Poll Activity — are containers actively polling?
Metrics Pipeline — what is landing in Prometheus?
Processing Queues — is ktranslate keeping up?
Upload Failures — are batches being dropped?
